capture.final_message:
View `Ordinal.type α (<)` as the ordinal encoding of the well-order on `α`, with `Ordinal.enum` providing the order isomorphism between its initial segment and `α`.

- For the first conjunct, transport the definition of `Order.IsSuccPrelimit` across `Ordinal.enum`. Saying that every rank below `type α` has a strictly larger rank still below it is exactly saying that every `x : α` has some `y > x`, i.e. `NoMaxOrder α`. The well-foundedness assumption is essential because it makes `Ordinal.type` and `Ordinal.enum` available.

- For the second conjunct, `h₀ : 0 < o` ensures that rank `0` belongs to the initial segment below `type (Ordinal.ToType o) = o`. Its image under `Ordinal.enum` is the least element of `Ordinal.ToType o`. To show it is below an arbitrary `a`, pull `a` back through the inverse order isomorphism and use that no ordinal rank is strictly below `0` (or equivalently that `0` is least), then transport the resulting comparison forward.

Thus organize the proof as the conjunction of the standard “successor-prelimit type iff no maximal element” characterization and the elementary fact that enumeration at ordinal rank zero yields the minimum element.
